tasks.title: Flight Recorder audit trail and explainability surface
tasks.goal: Close the gap between the current hash-chained audit/query surface and a compliance-grade flight recorder that can explain what each agent requested, how Guardrail resolved it, why it was allowed/required approval/blocked, what actually ran, what output was produced, and what files/resources changed.
tasks.comment: Created from the Flight Recorder gap review: current Guardrail audit has chain integrity, query, blocked/runtime events, and lane timelines, but does not yet provide one normalized per-run evidence record or the requested audit last/show/explain/blocked/timeline command family.
definition_of_done: Audit entries or linked run evidence record normalized agent_id, origin tool/client, requested action, declared recipe/tool, resolved command, approved manifest hash, sanitized input values, risk traits, decision enum, block/approval reason, actual execution result/output reference, and file/resource changes without leaking secrets.
Decision outcomes are explicit and queryable as allowed, approval_required, or blocked, with stable reason codes distinct from human-readable messages.

CLI surfaces exist for the operator workflows: guardrail audit last, guardrail audit show <run-id>, guardrail audit explain <run-id>, guardrail audit blocked, and guardrail audit timeline, with --json envelopes compatible with event schema versioning.
The implementation reuses the existing hash-chained audit log and/or linked evidence artifacts rather than introducing an unchained parallel truth source.

Proof covers allowed execution, approval-required noninteractive stop, policy/runtime blocked execution, denied interactive approval, failed execution with output reference, and at least one file/resource-change capture path.
constraints: Do not persist raw secrets, raw tokens, or unbounded stdout/stderr directly in audit rows; store bounded clips or content-addressed artifact references with hashes.
Do not silently change execution/approval policy while adding observability; separate recording changes from any new blocking behavior.
Keep existing guardrail audit verify/query compatibility or version the JSON response envelope if the shape changes.
Use stable machine reason codes for explain output; do not force consumers to parse prose.
Do not duplicate lane history/portfolio mechanisms; integrate or reference them from the audit timeline surface.

context.gap_summary: Current Guardrail audit has hash chaining, verify/query, blocked/execution events, and lane timelines. Missing: one per-run forensic evidence surface covering requested action, resolved command, manifest approval, inputs, risk traits, decision, output reference, and file/resource changes plus last/show/explain/blocked/timeline CLI workflows.
context.source_question: User requested a Flight Recorder for auditing and compliance after gap review on 2026-04-29.

Implementation tasks have explicit boundaries for approval handshake, runtime operations, audit, spawn, and mode switching.
Known contradictions from review are resolved before code work starts.
constraints: Do not implement RBAA/Auth code until the plan contradictions are resolved.
Keep static mode behavior unchanged unless a task explicitly changes the runtime contract.

context.notes: Plan repair package completed on feature/rbaa-auth-000; child tasks rbaa-auth-001..009 resolved in the plan.

tasks.title: Rebase RBAA/Auth plan on landed P0a/P0b/P0c
tasks.goal: Update the plan assumptions to reflect that Guardrail already has `src/authorization.js`, policy simulation, decision traces, and sovereign audit metadata.
definition_of_done: The prerequisite section states P0a/P0b/P0c are already landed where true.
Phase 0 is framed as adapting the existing `authorize(action, facts)` seam rather than creating a second seam.
Any stale confidence assumptions about P0a landing first are removed or rewritten.

context.notes: Plan now treats P0a/P0b/P0c as landed tracker items and extends the shipped authorization seam/trace/metadata contracts.

tasks.title: Define authorization action taxonomy and adapter contract
tasks.goal: Separate approval-time handshake decisions, runtime operation gates, simulation, escalation, and approval outcomes into one explicit adapter request/response contract.
definition_of_done: The plan names every adapter action family: approval handshake, runtime operation, recipe auth preflight, lane/session lifecycle, adapter preflight, and simulation if included.
The result contract covers `allow`, `deny`, `requires_escalation`, and `requires_approval` without breaking existing static callers.
The static adapter parity contract names which existing fields must remain stable.

context.review_findings: Existing `authorize()` is binary today; RBAA introduces non-binary outcomes that need status and exit-code mapping.
context.notes: Added adapter action taxonomy, normalized non-binary outcomes, and compact exit-code mapping.

tasks.title: Resolve static/rbaa manifest migration semantics
tasks.goal: Pick one consistent rule for static manifests under rbaa and rbaa manifests under static, then align migration text and tests.
definition_of_done: The plan no longer says rbaa manifests are both rejected under static and non-disruptive under static.
Mode isolation tests match the selected migration rule.
Rollback/reverse-migration behavior is explicit for operators.

context.review_findings: The current test plan and migration section conflict.
context.notes: Resolved migration as symmetric mode-scoped manifests/envelopes with no automatic reuse or backfill.

tasks.title: Inventory all audit and spawn surfaces before enforcement design
tasks.goal: Create the authoritative list of audit append paths and worker spawn paths that RBAA mode must cover.
definition_of_done: The plan lists every current `launchWorker()` call site and states whether envelope enforcement applies there.
The plan lists audit append helper surfaces and specifies how `authMode`, `decisionId`, and envelope fields are applied centrally.
The plan no longer claims four supervisor edits are enough if helper/executor paths remain uncovered.

context.review_findings: Envelope enforcement and audit fields are wider than the four top-level supervisors.
context.notes: Added inventory requirement for audit, approval/risk, lifecycle, runtime auth, and spawn/delegation surfaces.

tasks.title: Define auth-mode root, environment override, and process immutability
tasks.goal: Specify exactly which state directory owns auth-mode configuration across command, template, workflow, recipe, lane, and adapter surfaces.
definition_of_done: The plan names the canonical deployment-level auth-mode root and how surface-local state dirs relate to it.
Per-environment override lookup order is deterministic and testable.
Process-immutable resolution is defined for CLI and imported module usage.

context.review_findings: Current stateDir meanings vary by surface, so `<stateDir>/auth-mode.json` is ambiguous.
context.notes: Defined canonical authConfigRoot, per-environment override root, and process-immutable mode resolution.

tasks.title: Revise Phase 0 implementation slice
tasks.goal: Turn Phase 0 into a no-behavior-change adapter extraction behind the existing authorization seam with explicit architecture tests.
definition_of_done: Phase 0 says `authorize()` delegates to static adapter or equivalent without changing public call sites unless justified.

tasks.title: Gate rbaa activation until load-bearing enforcement exists
tasks.goal: Adjust phases so `auth-mode set rbaa` cannot create a cosmetic mode that mints envelopes before enforcement and identity binding are safe enough.
definition_of_done: The plan distinguishes internal adapter tests from operator-visible `auth-mode set rbaa` activation.
Activation prerequisites include envelope enforcement and the selected identity behavior.
Phase DoDs prevent envelope minting from being mistaken for completed RBAA enforcement.

context.review_findings: Phase 3 activation precedes Phase 4 enforcement and Phase 5 identity, creating a half-secure mode.
context.notes: Gated persistent rbaa activation until envelope enforcement and verifiable identity handling are load-bearing.

tasks.title: Specify envelope persistence, counters, and renewal state

approval_required_for: Any behavior that allows execution without host approval or approved request id
